add_brands.says: Mineralogical Record (Schuh bio-bibliography): founded 1833 in Freiberg, moved to Bonn 1850; 'this famous German mineral dealing firm' that 'became famous worldwide' and 'survives to the current time'; prize-winning maker and publisher of mineralogical/geological teaching collections and wooden crystal models (Lehrmittel)
add_brands.dept: minerals, rocks & teaching sets, crystal models

add_brands.says: Mineralogical Record biography: Barcelona dealer (1971/1986-2023), first Spanish dealer at the TGMS Main Show, 20+ best-specimen/display awards, one of the first three mineral dealers on the Internet (1996); closed 1 Oct 2023, archive continues as #MVM; historic/closed firm

Art & Antiques Magazine feature on fine minerals as natural art quotes Daniel Trinchillo, owner of Fine Minerals International (Edison NJ), as a leading dealer alongside Heritage Auctions and Bonhams; NYC gallery Mardani Fine Minerals is its flagship
Art & Antiques Magazine: Bonhams' fine minerals expert Claudia Florian runs mineral and gem sales (Bonhams Los Angeles), pioneered the '100-carat club' of cabinet gems

Wikipedia: Guido T. Poppe, Belgian malacologist and shell dealer (moved to the Philippines 2003), discovered 1000+ mollusc species, described 500+; his firm's journal Visaya is cited as 'Journal of Conchology Inc., Cebu'; Houston Museum of Natural Science exhibited 'Gems of the Sea: The Guido T. Poppe Collection' (standing only)
add_brands.cites: some shells traded are CITES-listed (Tridacnidae giant clams, Strombus/Aliger gigas queen conch, Nautilidae, stony/black corals): legality note needed

add_brands.says: 'Shellers from the Past and Present' biography (Conchology Inc. site, not Femorale's own): Marcus and José Coltro 'built Femorale into an internationally known shell business in São Paulo, active since 1989, now established in Italy'; many species named after the Coltros
add_brands.cites: shell dealer: CITES note as for Conchology, Inc.

add_brands.says: BRUTUS: oldest surviving Japanese insect specialist shop (founded 1971), 'the leader of Japan's insect shops', thousands of specimens plus specimen-making tools; publishes Gekkan Mushi, Japan's only general insect magazine. Nakano City tourism page (https://www.city.tokyo-nakano.lg.jp/kanko/machiaruki/mushi-sha_01.html) calls it a 'holy place' of Japan's distinctive insect-collecting culture
add_brands.cites: some butterflies (Ornithoptera, Troides, Teinopalpus, Bhutanitis) are CITES-listed: legality note

add_brands.n: Shiga Konchu Fukyusha (志賀昆虫普及社)
add_brands.says: Tokamachi city Kyororo science museum biography of founder Shiga Usuke ('father of Japanese insect collecting', 'Japan's No.1 insect dealer'): firm founded 1931; its headed stainless 'Shiga insect pins' took 20+ years to develop and are 'still used and loved worldwide'; also collecting tools; founder received the Medal with Yellow Ribbon (1974). Museum page used for standing only

Anadolu Agency: Rostec's Kaliningrad Amber Combine is 'the only enterprise in the world that mines amber on an industrial scale' (Yantarny holds most of Russia's ~90% share of extractable amber); sells raw amber nuggets and pieces with fossil inclusions; record 630 t in 2023

Darlington & Stockton Times: Whitby jet house founded by James Storr in 1860 (150th birthday 2010), uses only Whitby jet, owns a 21 ft piece of jet; recreated a Roman jet object for the Yorkshire Museum; owner says 'the best quality of all is found in Whitby'. Mainly jet jewellery: primary home A3, F6 for loose jet
add_brands.note: jewellery maker; tag A3 primarily, F6 only via jet
